questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake light, especially when the taillight is on. Other drivers may not see your brake light.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road shows:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly press it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: In a group ride, new riders should be:
questions.explanation: New riders should ride near the front, right behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.explanation: Ride slower at night and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use your high beam when there is no other traffic.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: If you wear a jacket while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool.
Keep the jacket on to protect yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect yourself.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. It also helps prevent dehydration in hot weather. Most riding jackets are designed to keep you from overheating.

questions.question: Before turning, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent power from changing in the middle of the turn.
Keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
Stop the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent power from changing in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. Shifting while turning can suddenly change power to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, how much you drink, and how fast you drink it. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A sign that your front tire is flat is when steering suddenly feels:
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: _________ of all crashes between a motorcycle and a car are caused by the driver not yielding the right-of-way to the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that drivers of larger vehicles will yield, even if they are required to by law.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This warning sign tells you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Your normal scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Always looking in the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in broad daylight. Always wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, pick a lane position that makes you most visible. Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. Slow down when approaching. Do not change your speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power to the rear wheel can cause a skid.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a full-face helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When preparing to ride with a passenger, tell the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Have your passenger wait to mount the motorcycle until after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and firmly hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
Pass more than one vehicle at the same time.

questions.explanation: You must complete all passes within the legal speed limit. Only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to weave over uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Shift down to a lower gear right away.
Ride in a zigzag pattern until you cross the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle starts to weave over metal bridge gratings, stay relaxed and go straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Change your lane position based on conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Be ready to change your lane position as road, traffic, and weather conditions change.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean toward the direction of the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean toward the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean toward the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, you should ride in:
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in the ______ of a lane.
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve
On the inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the stopped emergency vehicle extra space and continue with caution. Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see an emergency.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding decisions. What does "SEE" stand for?
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: Other drivers can usually see a motorcyclist best when riding in which lane position?
questions.explanation: When traffic allows, the center lane position is best because drivers can see you in their rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions require it.
